abstracts.abstract: Provides that a communication or attorney work product otherwise protected by the attorney-client privilege or which otherwise shall not be obtainable by another party shall not lose its privileged or unobtainable character solely as a result of it being produced by, transmitted to, processed by, stored on, or otherwise facilitated through an artificial intelligence technology; requires authorization from the client to utilize artificial intelligence.

bill.title: Relates to the use of artificial intelligence and attorney-client privilege and work product

posted_text:
🧠 NY A11723 — AI in Your Lawsuit? Attorneys Can Now Use It – With a Catch

New York is letting attorneys use artificial intelligence to help with your legal cases, but it comes with a big warning.

The bill says that communications protected by attorney-client privilege – like advice and legal documents – won’t lose that protection just because an AI system processed them, as long as the advice was given in confidence.

However, attorneys *must* get written permission from you to use AI, and they have to explain the risks, including the possibility of the AI making up false information or offering bad legal advice.

You’re not liable for mistakes the AI makes, unless you’re representing yourself, and attorneys can’t use AI to bypass human review.

If an attorney’s form allows for AI without human oversight, the form is automatically void.

Sept. 16, 2026: Referred to Judiciary.

🔗 Read the full bill: https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/bills/2025/A11723
